gloss: to hold up to the light; to leave a gap

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {透|す}かしていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to hold up to the light; to look through
definitions.explanation: To hold something up against a light source in order to see through it, often to check for watermarks, flaws, or hidden features.

definitions.gloss: to leave a gap; to thin out
definitions.explanation: To create space between things, such as thinning out branches or leaving gaps for ventilation.

examples.english: I held the paper up to the light to look at it.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{札|さつ}→お札：19147_osatsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{透|す}かす⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、{透|す}かし⟦{模様|もよう}→模様：03635_moyou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: If you hold a banknote up to the light, you can see the watermark.

examples.japanese: ⟦{木漏|こも}れ{日|び}→木漏れ日：07683_komorebi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{葉|は}→葉：02241_ha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{透|す}かして⟦{差|さ}し{込|こ}んでいた→差し込む：04235_sashikomu⟧。
examples.english: Sunlight was filtering through the leaves.

examples.japanese: ⟦{枝|えだ}→枝：02181_eda⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{透|す}かして⟦{風通|かぜとお}し→風通し：09032_kazetooshi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Thin out the branches to improve air circulation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{前髪|まえがみ}→前髪：19004_maegami⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{透|す}かして⟦{軽|かる}く→軽い：00785_karui⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。
examples.english: I had my bangs thinned out to make them lighter.
If you don't thin out the garden plant's leaves, it becomes more susceptible to insects.

notes:
Godan verb (す・⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧・す). The transitive counterpart of ⟦{透|す}ける→透ける：04568_sukeru⟧ (to be transparent, to show through).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{光|ひかり}→光：01707_hikari⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{透|す}かす (to hold up to the light)
- {透|す}かして⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧ (to look at something by holding it up to light)
- {透|す}かし⟦{模様|もよう}→模様：03635_moyou⟧ (watermark pattern)
- ⟦{枝|えだ}→枝：02181_eda⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{透|す}かす (to thin out branches)
- ⟦{髪|かみ}→髪：02196_kami⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{透|す}かす (to thin out hair)

Sense 1 is the more commonly encountered meaning. The connection between the two senses is the idea of allowing light or air to pass through by creating openings.
